memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'If many years remain, they must pay for their redemption a larger share of
the price paid for them. If only a few years remain until the Year of
Jubilee, they are to compute that and pay for their redemption accordingly.
They are to be treated as workers hired from year to year; you must see to it
that those to whom they owe service do not rule over them ruthlessly'"
- Lev 25:51-53 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The redemption price was calculated fairly, based on how many years remained
until Jubilee. Nobody could inflate the cost to trap the person or profit
unjustly from their misfortune. And once more — for the third time in this
section — comes the command: do not rule over them ruthlessly.

God's concern for fairness runs right down to the arithmetic. The exact price
had to be honest. Even in the fine detail of a financial calculation, God
required justice and forbade exploitation.

Dear reader, this reminds us that God cares about the details, not just the
grand principles. It is easy to affirm fairness in the abstract while
shading the specifics in our favour. God closes that gap. Honest scales, fair
prices, and no ruthlessness — right down to the numbers.

Consider by contrast the price of our redemption. It was not calculated to be
as small as possible. It was the highest price ever paid. Peter says we were
redeemed not with perishable things like silver or gold, but with the
precious blood of Christ (1 Pet 1:18-19). Paul says we were bought at a price
(1 Cor 6:20).

Our redemption was not cheap, and it was not partial. Christ paid in full.
There is no remaining balance for you to settle. The price was counted out
completely on the cross.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I honest in the details, or only in principle?
2. Do I grasp the full price that was paid for my redemption?
3. Is there any way I am still trying to pay a debt Christ has settled?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that my redemption was paid in full by the precious blood
of Christ, with no remaining balance. Make me honest in every detail, as You
are. Amen.
